final_message:
The oracle provider now emits `Arch` only where the architecture actually changes the fix, and it advertises the new 1.1.1 schema. All 913 unit tests pass. The full-repo run also had 15 `tests/quality` failures from a missing `yardstick` module, which I didn't touch.

- **Parser** (`oval_parser.py`): it now reads the `Oracle Linux arch is X` criterion and tags each package version with that arch. For each package, if every architecture lists the same set of versions, it emits one arch-less `FixedIn` per version. That covers a single shared fix and several rebuilds that all ship everywhere. Otherwise it emits one entry per (version, arch) with `"Arch"` set. For ELSA-2022-4803 that gives `8.24.0-57.0.4.el7_9.3` for aarch64 and `8.24.0-57.0.1.el7_9.3` for x86_64.
- **Schema:** `schema/vulnerability/os/schema-1.1.1.json` is 1.1.0 plus an optional string `FixedIn.Arch`. Only the oracle provider uses `OSSchema(version="1.1.1")`, so other providers stay on 1.1.0. I did not change `OS_SCHEMA_VERSION`.
- **Snapshots and tests:** I updated the oracle snapshot schema URLs to 1.1.1. I added `test_parse_arch`, which covers the three cases: arch-differentiated, shared fix, and multiple rebuilds on all arches.
- **Running tests:** The tests only ran with `PYTHONPATH=src`, because `vunnel` isn't importable from `.venv` otherwise. The command in CLAUDE.md fails at conftest import without it.
- **Packages missing on some arches:** The "same on every arch" check compares against the arches seen across the whole advisory. A package that appears under only some arches therefore keeps its `Arch` entries.

I also wrote `answer.json` in the repo root with the one-sentence summary.

def _arch_definition(arch_versions):
    groups = ""
    for arch, versions in arch_versions.items():
        crits = "".join(
            f'<criterion test_ref="t" comment="rsyslog is earlier than {v}"/>' for v in versions
        )
        groups += (
            f'<criteria operator="AND"><criterion test_ref="t" comment="Oracle Linux arch is {arch}"/>'
            f'<criteria operator="OR">{crits}</criteria></criteria>'
        )
    return f"""<oval_definitions xmlns="http://oval.mitre.org/XMLSchema/oval-definitions-5">
<definitions>
<definition id="d" version="1" class="patch">
<metadata>
<title> ELSA-2022-4803: rsyslog security update (MODERATE) </title>
<affected family="unix"><platform>Oracle Linux 7</platform></affected>
<reference source="elsa" ref_id="ELSA-2022-4803" ref_url="https://linux.oracle.com/errata/ELSA-2022-4803.html"/>
<description> d </description>
<advisory><severity>MODERATE</severity><issued date="2022-06-01"/></advisory>
</metadata>
<criteria operator="AND">
<criterion test_ref="t" comment="Oracle Linux 7 is installed"/>
<criteria operator="OR">{groups}</criteria>
</criteria>
</definition>
</definitions>
</oval_definitions>
"""


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("arch_versions", "expected"),
    [
        # arch differentiates the fix
        (
            {"aarch64": ["8.24.0-57.0.4.el7_9.3"], "x86_64": ["8.24.0-57.0.1.el7_9.3"]},
            [("8.24.0-57.0.1.el7_9.3", "x86_64"), ("8.24.0-57.0.4.el7_9.3", "aarch64")],
        ),
        # one fix shared by every arch
        (
            {"aarch64": ["8.24.0-57.el7_9.3"], "x86_64": ["8.24.0-57.el7_9.3"]},
            [("8.24.0-57.el7_9.3", None)],
        ),
        # several rebuilds, each shipping for all arches
        (
            {"aarch64": ["1-1.el7", "1-2.el7"], "x86_64": ["1-1.el7", "1-2.el7"]},
            [("1-1.el7", None), ("1-2.el7", None)],
        ),
    ],
)
def test_parse_arch(tmpdir, arch_versions, expected):
    path = tmpdir / "oval.xml"
    path.write(_arch_definition(arch_versions))
    subject = parser.Parser(workspace=workspace.Workspace(tmpdir, "test", create=True))

    vuln_dict = subject._parse_oval_data(str(path), subject.config)

    _, record = vuln_dict[("ELSA-2022-4803", "ol:7")]
    fixed_in = record["Vulnerability"]["FixedIn"]
    assert sorted((f["Version"], f.get("Arch")) for f in fixed_in) == sorted(expected)
    assert all(f["Name"] == "rsyslog" for f in fixed_in)
EOF
